```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo       = TRUE,
  message    = FALSE,
  warning    = FALSE,
  fig.width  = 10,
  fig.height = 6
)

show_table <- function(df, caption = NULL, align = NULL, bold_col = 1,
                       mono_col = NULL, highlight_last = FALSE,
                       scroll = FALSE) {
  if (!requireNamespace("kableExtra", quietly = TRUE))
    return(knitr::kable(df, caption = caption, align = align, digits = 1))
  k <- knitr::kable(df, format = "html", caption = caption, align = align,
                    digits = 1) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
      full_width        = FALSE,
      position          = "left"
    )
  if (!is.null(bold_col))
    k <- kableExtra::column_spec(k, bold_col, bold = TRUE)
  if (!is.null(mono_col))
    k <- kableExtra::column_spec(k, mono_col, monospace = TRUE, color = "black")
  if (highlight_last)
    k <- kableExtra::row_spec(k, nrow(df), bold = TRUE, background = "#f0f7ff")
  if (scroll)
    k <- kableExtra::scroll_box(k, width = "100%")
  k
}
```

# Overview

Feature-grouping tools such as CAMERA, RAMClustR or MZmine ion identity
networking combine the features of one compound (adducts, isotopes,
in-source fragments) into groups. Untargeted metabolomics has no absolute
ground truth for these groups. MS1Match therefore provides a
**compound-centric reference feature set**: the features it assigned to library
compounds, stratified by evidence tier. This vignette evaluates the groups
of another tool against that reference set.

**This vignette does not run MS1Match.** It starts from a finished MS1Match
result:

- for an xcms feature table, see vignette *2a. MS1Match workflow: StM14*;
- for an MZmine or other CSV feature table, or data without MS2, see
  vignette *2c. MS1Match with other inputs*.

MS1Match is the reference here, not one of the tools being compared.
Evaluating MS1Match's own groups against its own reference set would be
circular.

The examples use the StM14 data shipped with the package, with CAMERA and
RAMClustR as example tools. The last section collects the calls for your own
data.

```{r packages}
library(MS1Match)
library(dplyr)
```

# What you need

```{r tab-inputs, echo = FALSE}
show_table(data.frame(
  Input = c("Feature table", "MS1Match result", "Grouping result"),
  `Where it comes from` = c(
    "The feature table MS1Match was run on",
    "anno_result from join_annotation_results() (vignette 2a or 2c)",
    "Your grouping tool, run on the same feature table"),
  check.names = FALSE), align = c("l", "l"))
```

**The one requirement:** MS1Match and the grouping tool must work on the
**same feature table**, so that both refer to a feature by the same id (for
xcms `FT0001`, `FT0002`, ...).

```{.workflow}
                 ┌─> MS1Match ──────> anno_result ──┐   (vignette 2a / 2c)
                 │                                  │
feature table ──>┤                                  ├─> evaluate_grouping()
                 │                                  │   (this vignette)
                 └─> grouping tool ─> grouping ─────┘
                     (CAMERA, RAMClustR, ...)
```

The evaluation has five steps:

1. Load the feature table and the MS1Match result.
2. Convert the grouping result into a standard table.
3. Check that both used the same feature table.
4. Evaluate one or several tools.
5. Read the results.

# Step 1 — Load the feature table and the MS1Match result

For StM14, the feature table is the xcms result `StM14_out.rds`. MS1Match,
CAMERA and RAMClustR were all run on it. `anno_result` was saved at the end
of vignette 2a.

```{r load-ms1match}
data_dir <- system.file("extdata", "RDS_files", "StM14", package = "MS1Match")

StM14_out     <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "StM14_out.rds"))
feature_table <- StM14_out$ft

anno_result   <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "anno_result_StM14.rds"))
```

The evaluation uses two tables of `anno_result`:

- `export_feature_compound_summary`: the reference features, one row per
  feature × compound;
- `export_reduced_anno_table`: used to find each compound's Tier 1a
  `[M+H]+` anchor.

# Step 2 — Convert the grouping result into a standard table

Every tool is reduced to one row per feature with these columns:

```{r tab-columns, echo = FALSE}
show_table(data.frame(
  Column  = c("feature_name", "group", "mz", "rt"),
  Meaning = c("feature id, as in the MS1Match feature table",
              "group / cluster id; NA = feature not grouped",
              "m/z of the feature, used to verify the feature table",
              "retention time in seconds (optional)")),
  align = c("l", "l"), mono_col = 1)
```

The table must list **every** feature the tool processed, including the
ones it did not group (`group = NA`). The converters below do this.

Pick the subsection that matches your tool.

## CAMERA

Use the peak list from `CAMERA::getPeaklist()`. If it has no `feature_name`
column, `camera_to_grouping()` creates xcms-style ids from the row order.
To be explicit, pass `feature_names = rownames(featureDefinitions(xdata))`.

```{r camera}
CAMERA_peaklist <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "CAMERA_annotated_StM14_FT.csv"))

grouping_camera <- camera_to_grouping(CAMERA_peaklist)
head(grouping_camera)
```

## RAMClustR

Pass the object returned by `RAMClustR::ramclustR()`. Features RAMClustR did
not cluster (`featclus = 0`) get `group = NA`.

```{r ramclustr-check, include = FALSE}
rc_path <- file.path(data_dir, "RC_StM14.rds")
has_rc  <- file.exists(rc_path)
```

```{r ramclustr, eval = has_rc}
RC <- readRDS(rc_path)

grouping_ramclustr <- ramclustr_to_grouping(RC)
head(grouping_ramclustr)
```

## MZmine

This applies when MS1Match was run on an MZmine feature table imported with
`read_mzmine_feature_table()` (vignette 2c). Take the grouping from the same
MZmine full feature table: `feature_group` (correlation grouping) or
`ion_identities:iin_id` (ion identity networks).

`mzmine_to_grouping()` applies the same conversions as the import:

- MZmine `id` becomes an `FT0001`-style id;
- RT is converted from minutes to seconds;
- features removed by the import's detection filter are dropped.

MZmine numbers its groups from 0, so `0` is a real group. Set
`unassigned = ""` so that only empty cells count as "not grouped".

```{r mzmine, eval = FALSE}
mzmine_file <- system.file("extdata", "MZmine_feature_table", "StM14_MZmine_export",
                           "StM14_mzmine_full_feature_table.csv",
                           package = "MS1Match")

ft_mzmine  <- read_mzmine_feature_table(mzmine_file)   # table MS1Match ran on
mzmine_raw <- read.csv(mzmine_file, check.names = FALSE)

grouping_mzmine <- mzmine_to_grouping(
  mzmine_raw,
  group_col     = "ion_identities:iin_id",   # or "feature_group"
  keep_features = ft_mzmine$feature_name,
  unassigned    = ""                         # MZmine group ids start at 0
)
```

## Any other tool

This covers a tool that ran on the MS1Match feature table and exports its
result in its own format, e.g. a CSV. Name its feature-id and group columns:

```{r other-tool, eval = FALSE}
my_result <- read.csv("my_tool_groups.csv")

grouping_mytool <- prepare_grouping_table(
  my_result,
  feature_col = "feature_id",   # your tool's feature-id column (FT0001, ...)
  group_col   = "cluster",      # your tool's group column
  mz_col      = "mz",           # your tool's m/z column (required for the check)
  rt_col      = "rt",           # optional
  rt_unit     = "sec",          # or "min"; converted to seconds
  unassigned  = c("0", "")      # values meaning "not grouped"; check whether
                                #   your tool uses 0 as a real group id
)
```

### The tool's output has no feature ids

If the tool exported m/z and RT but no feature ids, give each row the id of
the feature with the same m/z and RT in the MS1Match feature table. The tool
ran on that table, so the values are identical.

```{r other-tool-noid, eval = FALSE}
my_result <- assign_feature_names(
  my_result, feature_table,
  mz_col  = "mz",
  rt_col  = "rt",
  rt_unit = "min"            # unit of my_result$rt; converted to seconds here
)

# RT is now in seconds: keep the default rt_unit = "sec"
grouping_mytool <- prepare_grouping_table(
  my_result, group_col = "cluster", mz_col = "mz", rt_col = "rt")
```

Do not create ids by sorting the grouping result. Sorted ids only agree with
the feature table if both hold exactly the same rows in the same order.
Matching on m/z and RT also works for subsets.

### The groups are in the feature table itself

Some pre-processing software (e.g. MZmine, MS-DIAL) exports one table that
holds both the features and a group / cluster column. That table serves
both branches:

1. Run MS1Match on it as described in vignette 2c. This gives `ft` and
   `anno_result`. (For MZmine tables, use `mzmine_to_grouping()` above
   instead.)
2. Take the grouping from the same `ft`:

```{r own-table-groups, eval = FALSE}
grouping_mytool <- prepare_grouping_table(
  ft,
  group_col = "cluster",                    # the group column of your table
  mz_col    = "mzmed", rt_col = "rtmed"     # column names in ft; check names(ft)
)
```

3. Continue with Step 3, using `feature_table = ft`.

## If the feature tables differ

Two different feature tables cannot be compared. A feature in one table has
no defined counterpart in the other, so "same group as the anchor" has no
meaning. Run both on one table instead:

- **Run the grouping tool on the MS1Match feature table.** For example, give
  CAMERA, RAMClustR or cliqueMS the same xcms object that MS1Match used.
- **Or run MS1Match on the grouping tool's feature table.** For example,
  import an MZmine feature table with `read_mzmine_feature_table()`, run
  MS1Match on it (vignette 2c), and evaluate the MZmine grouping with
  `mzmine_to_grouping()`.

# Step 3 — Check that both used the same feature table

The check answers yes or no. Every feature id shared by the MS1Match result,
the grouping table and the feature table must have **the same m/z** (and RT,
where available). Feature ids alone are not enough, because separate xcms
runs all name their features `FT0001`, `FT0002`, ...

```{r feature-match}
check_feature_match(anno_result, grouping_camera, feature_table)
```

If the answer is NO, the printout lists the first mismatching features and
the reason: m/z differs, RT differs, or a reference feature is missing from
the feature table. `evaluate_grouping()` runs the same check and stops on NO.

**Subsets are allowed.** One table may be a subset of the other, e.g.
MS1Match run on an RT-truncated feature table and the grouping tool on the
full one. The evaluation then uses only the features present in both. The
printout reports how many were excluded on each side.

A feature missing from the grouping table is treated as outside the shared
feature table, not as Ref-unassigned.

# Step 4 — Evaluate

## One tool

```{r evaluate}
eval_camera <- evaluate_grouping(
  anno_result,
  grouping_camera,
  tool_name     = "CAMERA",
  feature_table = feature_table,
  rt_window     = c(60, 1200)
)
eval_camera
```

`rt_window` only restricts features *outside* the reference set. It keeps
their counts comparable between tools: here, MS1Match was run on features
within 60–1200 s. Reference features are always evaluated.

## Several tools

Every tool is evaluated with the same call; only the grouping table and the
name change. Put the grouping tables in a named list:

```{r evaluate-many}
groupings <- list(CAMERA = grouping_camera)
if (has_rc) groupings$RAMClustR <- grouping_ramclustr
# groupings$MyTool <- grouping_mytool     # any table from Step 2

evals <- lapply(names(groupings), function(tool)
  evaluate_grouping(anno_result, groupings[[tool]],
                    tool_name     = tool,
                    feature_table = feature_table,
                    rt_window     = c(60, 1200)))
names(evals) <- names(groupings)
```

# Step 5 — Results

Each evaluation contains three tables:

```{r tab-outputs, echo = FALSE}
show_table(data.frame(
  Table = c("benchmark", "status_counts", "full_table"),
  Content = c(
    "One row per tier: counts and % of reference features per status",
    "Status counts over all features, including those outside the reference set",
    "One row per reference feature × compound, plus one row per feature outside the reference set")),
  align = c("l", "l"), mono_col = 1)
```

## Tier benchmark

```{r benchmark}
show_table(eval_camera$benchmark,
           caption = "CAMERA: tier-stratified benchmark (StM14)",
           highlight_last = TRUE, scroll = TRUE)   # last row = Total
```

## Status over all features

```{r status-counts}
show_table(eval_camera$status_counts,
           caption = "CAMERA: reference-relative status of all features")
```

## Comparing tools

```{r compare}
show_table(do.call(compare_grouping, unname(evals)),
           caption = "Status (%) per tier and tool",
           highlight_last = TRUE, scroll = TRUE)
```

## Single compounds

Use `full_table` to see how a tool grouped the features of one compound:

```{r inspect}
eval_camera$full_table %>%
  filter(Compound_name == Compound_name[1]) %>%
  select(feature_name, Compound_name, tier, group, anchor_group, ref_status)
```

## Per-feature overview of all standards

One row per reference feature × compound (here: all features MS1Match
assigned to the 14 StM14 standards), with:

- the MS1Match evidence: tier and annotation;
- per tool: the feature's group, the anchor's group and the reference
  status (`NA` group = the tool did not group the feature);
- for CAMERA also its own isotope and adduct labels.

The statuses are taken from `evals` (Step 4), so they match the benchmark.

```{r feature-overview}
# MS1Match evidence per reference row
evidence <- anno_result$export_feature_compound_summary %>%
  select(feature_name, Compound_name, Lib_group, reference_tier,
         any_of(c("grp_anno_match", "exp_anno_match", "iso_annotation"))) %>%
  mutate(MS1Match_anno = coalesce(na_if(grp_anno_match, ""),
                                  na_if(exp_anno_match, ""))) %>%
  select(-any_of(c("grp_anno_match", "exp_anno_match")))

# group, anchor group and status per tool, prefixed with the tool name
tool_cols <- function(tool) {
  evals[[tool]]$full_table %>%
    filter(!is.na(Compound_name)) %>%
    select(feature_name, Compound_name, Lib_group,
           !!paste0(tool, "_group")        := group,
           !!paste0(tool, "_anchor_group") := anchor_group,
           !!paste0(tool, "_ref_status")   := ref_status)
}

feature_overview <- Reduce(
  function(acc, tool) left_join(acc, tool_cols(tool),
                                by = c("feature_name", "Compound_name", "Lib_group")),
  names(evals),
  evidence %>% filter(feature_name %in% evals[[1]]$full_table$feature_name)
)

# CAMERA's own labels
camera_labels <- CAMERA_peaklist %>%
  select(feature_name, any_of(c("isotopes", "adduct"))) %>%
  rename_with(~ paste0("CAMERA_", .x), -feature_name) %>%
  mutate(across(-feature_name, ~ na_if(trimws(as.character(.x)), "")))

feature_overview <- feature_overview %>%
  left_join(feature_table %>% select(feature_name, mzmed, rtmed), by = "feature_name") %>%
  left_join(camera_labels, by = "feature_name") %>%
  relocate(Compound_name, feature_name, mzmed, rtmed, reference_tier,
           MS1Match_anno, any_of("iso_annotation")) %>%
  arrange(Compound_name, rtmed, mzmed)

feature_overview
```

Per standard: how many of its reference features each tool grouped with the
anchor, split from it, or left ungrouped.

```{r feature-overview-summary}
status_summary <- function(tool) {
  st <- feature_overview[[paste0(tool, "_ref_status")]]
  feature_overview %>%
    mutate(.st = st) %>%
    group_by(Compound_name) %>%
    summarise(
      !!paste0(tool, "_confirmed")   := sum(.st == "Ref-confirmed",   na.rm = TRUE),
      !!paste0(tool, "_conflicting") := sum(.st == "Ref-conflicting", na.rm = TRUE),
      !!paste0(tool, "_unassigned")  := sum(.st %in% c("Ref-unassigned",
                                                        "Ref-unassigned (no-anchor)")),
      .groups = "drop")
}

per_standard <- Reduce(
  function(acc, tool) left_join(acc, status_summary(tool), by = "Compound_name"),
  names(evals),
  feature_overview %>% count(Compound_name, name = "n_features")
) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_features))

show_table(per_standard,
           caption = "Reference features per standard and their status per tool",
           scroll = TRUE)
```

```{r feature-overview-export, eval = FALSE}
write.csv(feature_overview, "StM14_feature_overview.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
write.csv(per_standard,     "StM14_per_standard.csv",     row.names = FALSE)
```

# Reading the output

For each compound, the Tier 1a `[M+H]+` feature is the **anchor**; the group
the tool assigns to it is the compound's expected group. Every reference
compound has an anchor by construction. Each reference feature gets the
first status that applies, in this order:

```{r tab-status, echo = FALSE}
show_table(data.frame(
  Status = c("Ref-unassigned (no-anchor)", "Ref-unassigned",
             "Ref-confirmed", "Ref-conflicting",
             "Ref-unmatched, co-grouped", "Ref-unmatched, unrelated"),
  Meaning = c(
    "The tool did not group the compound's anchor; none of its features can be evaluated",
    "The anchor is grouped, this feature is not",
    "Same group as its compound's anchor",
    "Different group than its compound's anchor",
    "Feature outside the reference set, in a group with a compound anchor (possible over-grouping)",
    "Feature outside the reference set, in a group without an anchor, or in no group")),
  align = c("l", "l"))
```

The first four statuses apply to reference features and make up the tier
benchmark. The last two apply to features outside the reference set and
appear only in `status_counts` and `full_table`.

The benchmark also reports **coverage** (`pct_grouped`): the share of
reference features the tool grouped at all. Tools that group every feature
(e.g. CAMERA) have 100 % coverage and always 0 Ref-unassigned and 0
Ref-unassigned (no-anchor).

A further status, *Not evaluable*, appears only if a compound's anchor is
missing from the shared feature table (e.g. cut off by an RT window). It
should be 0; `evaluate_grouping()` warns otherwise.

# Using your own data

The same calls, collected. Replace the three inputs:

```{r own-data, eval = FALSE}
# Inputs
feature_table <- my_xcms_result$ft                 # the table MS1Match ran on
anno_result   <- readRDS("my_anno_result.rds")     # from vignette 2a / 2c
grouping      <- camera_to_grouping(getPeaklist(my_xsa))
                 # or ramclustr_to_grouping(RC), mzmine_to_grouping(...),
                 # or prepare_grouping_table(...)

# Check, evaluate
check_feature_match(anno_result, grouping, feature_table)   # must YES

res <- evaluate_grouping(anno_result, grouping,
                         tool_name     = "MyTool",
                         feature_table = feature_table,
                         rt_window     = c(60, 1200))
res

# Export
write.csv(res$benchmark,     "MyTool_benchmark.csv",     row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(res$status_counts, "MyTool_status_counts.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(res$full_table,    "MyTool_full_table.csv",    row.names = FALSE)
```

To export all tools from Step 4 at once:

```{r export-many, eval = FALSE}
for (tool in names(evals)) {
  write.csv(evals[[tool]]$benchmark,
            paste0(tool, "_benchmark.csv"),  row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(evals[[tool]]$full_table,
            paste0(tool, "_full_table.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}
```

# Optional: CAMERA adduct annotation accuracy

Besides groups, CAMERA assigns adduct labels. For Tier 1a features, their
coverage and accuracy are computed with CAMERA-specific functions. These
join on `feature_name` only and do not repeat the feature-table check. Run
them only after Step 3 has said YES.

```{r camera-annotation, eval = FALSE}
eval_full     <- build_eval_full(anno_result$export_feature_compound_summary,
                                 CAMERA_ft = CAMERA_peaklist)
anchors       <- build_anchors(eval_full,
                               full_anno = anno_result$export_reduced_anno_table)
anno_accuracy <- build_anno_accuracy(eval_full, anchors, ppm_tol = 10)
anno_accuracy$summary
```

The full CAMERA analysis (pcgroup purity, adduct confusion, case studies) is
in `analysis/StM14_CAMERA_evaluation.Rmd` in the GitHub repository.
